decisions.reason: With row-major matrices, changing to i-k-j makes the inner j loop access C[i][j] contiguously and reuse A[i][k], whereas the current inner i loop uses strided accesses.

The supplied static evidence identifies stack-resident accumulator traffic; a smaller 2x2 tile reduces accumulator pressure and is more likely to keep accumulators in registers than increasing the tile or reverting to repeated scalar C updates.

The current k-j-i order makes the inner i loop access C and A with row-stride jumps; changing to i-k-j makes the inner j accesses contiguous and directly targets the extremely high load-replay and MemNotReadyStall counts without relying on undocumented thresholds.

Static evidence identifies stack-resident accumulator traffic in the 4x4 kernel. A 2x2 tile reduces accumulator register pressure and is the action most likely to keep accumulators in registers; increasing to 8x8 would aggravate spills, while replacing tiling with a scalar update discards useful reuse.

The row-major inner-i traversal is strided for both C[i][j] and A[i][k], matching the extreme replay and memory-not-ready evidence; testing i-k-j directly makes j contiguous and should reduce stalls and cycles.

The regression boundary is unknown, so stack traffic alone does not justify shrinking; profiling the larger adjacent tile tests whether added reuse and ILP outweigh accumulator pressure, with adoption conditional on lower final cycles and monitored instruction, data-array, and stack costs.
